policy.attackRule: non-contact, non-graphic, no injury or gore
policy.publicationRule: publish only independently reviewed full frames or documented derivatives made exclusively from accepted source frames

reviewMethod.manualReview: every decoded frame at original resolution plus transition-adjacent frame comparisons
reviewMethod.contactSheets: navigation aids only; they do not replace full-frame or playback review
reviewMethod.postProcessing: deterministic trim, clone hold, frame repetition, forward/reverse ordering, and faststart remux only; no optical-flow interpolation

tyrannosaurus-rex-restrained-vocal-displ.finding: The full clip preserved the animal but produced too little visible jaw motion to answer the larger-motion request.

ankylosaurus-magniventris-fern-chew-f81-.finding: The head drifted while the feeding action remained too subtle; it was retained only as rejected process evidence.

tyrannosaurus-rex-triceratops-noncontact.finding: The Tyrannosaurus bowed and drifted toward a frontal morph after roughly frame 55, so no portion was published.

tyrannosaurus-rex-strong-vocal-display-f.rejectionReason: Later frames enlarged the gape and moved the head toward the top edge beyond the conservative motion-only gate.
tyrannosaurus-rex-strong-vocal-display-f.derivativeMethod: accepted frames 0-16, cloned turnaround hold, deterministic 2x temporal repetition, and reverse return; no optical flow
tyrannosaurus-rex-strong-vocal-display-f.finding: Published as a silent large jaw-opening comparison with the full head, neck, body, limbs, and tail retained.

ankylosaurus-magniventris-strong-fern-bi.derivativeMethod: video-stream copy with embedded ComfyUI prompt preservation and faststart container layout; no frame transform
ankylosaurus-magniventris-strong-fern-bi.finding: Two readable feeding cycles passed with four grounded legs, one continuous tail, and one integrated club; fine skull-surface variation remains a stated limitation.

tyrannosaurus-rex-triceratops-strong-non.rejectionReason: Later frames accumulated Tyrannosaurus leg and tail drift and increasing animal overlap risk.
tyrannosaurus-rex-triceratops-strong-non.derivativeMethod: accepted frames 0-24 forward and reverse, followed by frames 0-16 forward and reverse, trimmed to 81 frames; no optical flow
tyrannosaurus-rex-triceratops-strong-non.finding: Published as a non-contact pressure feint rather than a bite; both animals remain on separate banks with no collision, injury, or gore.
